doc.title: Jane Ira Bloom interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 3, 1998

title: Upcoming gigs and tour planning
summary: MoMA, her trio and quartet, Australia tour planning, and pricing as a business person.

venues.name: Einstein Planetarium, National Air and Space Museum

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: What’s the immediate future for you as far as upcoming gigs, concerts?

Museum of Modern Art in New York this coming month. Continuing to play with my trio with Bobby Previte on drums, Cameron Brown will be playing bass and sometimes Mark Dresser plays bass. Finishing a recording for Arabesque that’s coming up this spring, I’ve been doing some quartet recording, that also involved Fred Hersch on piano, Mark Dresser on bass and Bobby Previte on drums. This was the group that played Sweet Basil’s last year, and just raised the bandstand it was so wonderful. Anyway, what else am I up to? Planning a tour for January 1999, this is how far in advance the real world of jazz musicians has to think, I’ve been invited to play at the Melbourne Jazz Festival and the Sydney Jazz Festival in Australia, and preparing and find funding to get over there and do all that. All kinds of things are in the air.
Are you able to take your own group when you go?

Take a trio. Yeah take bass and drums with me. Planning a concert at the Einstein Planetarium down at the National Air and Space Museum. That’s also in the works probably for the fall. I mean it’s not like the old days where you get a gig and you show up, next night — lot of long term planning’s involved in being a jazz musician now. Different, huh?
Yeah, different, and also calculating what you have to charge in 1999 — in January of 1999 to go to Australia, what’s a fair price for me to ask to go over there.
Oh and it varies from country to country, yeah. A whole lot of factors. You have to be a business person as well as a musician and a lot of things, a lot of balls you’ve got to keep in the air.
You and your husband. Constantly juggling.
Sure. Sure. It’s life in the arts.
